gaps.sentence: Do I ___ to bring my own towel, or is one provided?
gaps.hint: a question about necessity with do
gaps.explanation: Questions about necessity use 'do ... have to': have to bring.

gaps.sentence: You ___ better take some cash — the stall does not take cards.
gaps.explanation: 'Had better' warns about a sensible action: had better take.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ leave the examination room without permission.
gaps.explanation: Formal rules use 'may not' (or 'must not') to deny permission: may not leave.

gaps.sentence: He ___ be hungry — he has just eaten a three-course meal.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' rules out the possibility based on evidence: can't be hungry.

gaps.sentence: ___ we need to book, or can we just turn up?
gaps.explanation: 'Need to' is a normal verb, so questions take 'do': Do we need.

gaps.sentence: You ___ use my office while I am on holiday.
I ___ work late every Wednesday this month; it is a new company policy.
gaps.hint: obligation imposed by an external rule
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' expresses obligation imposed by external rules: have to work.

gaps.sentence: You ___ to see that exhibition before it closes — it is outstanding.
gaps.hint: a strong recommendation with ought to
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' recommends something strongly: ought to see.
